messages.policy.title: A simulated storefront for local testing.
messages.policy.description: Products, prices, shipping, tax, and payment are illustrative. No card details, addresses, names, or email addresses are collected. Your bag stays in this browser; guest order access is held in memory and server-mode sessions stay in this tab.
messages.footer.credit: Local product photography from Unsplash. No visitor analytics.
messages.privacy.title: Privacy for a local test storefront.
messages.privacy.introduction: This fictional local storefront is not a live shop. It does not accept real payments or ship products.
messages.privacy.cartStorage: The bag is stored in this browser using product IDs and quantities only. It can be cleared by removing bag items or clearing this site's browser storage.
messages.privacy.noPersonalInfo: Checkout asks for no name, email address, postal address, customer account, or card information. Both data modes use a server-issued synthetic role session.
messages.privacy.accessKey: This tab stores a short-lived API-issued synthetic session token in sessionStorage. The API stores only its hash and checks the session before allowing an order to be created or viewed.
messages.privacy.analytics: The app does not set analytics cookies or send usage events. Product photos are bundled locally in the frontend.
messages.privacy.paymentsDescription: Every item, price, shipping amount, promo code, and tax setting is synthetic. The backend records a simulated payment status; no payment provider is contacted and no money moves. Do not enter real personal or payment information.
messages.privacy.localDataDescription: Synthetic orders and inventory are stored by the backend on the machine running the app. In the default local profile this uses a file-backed development database. Resetting that data is an operator action; this page does not offer a destructive reset control.
messages.privacy.callout: This notice describes the current local test storefront, not a production privacy policy or legal compliance certification. A public commercial storefront would need a separate privacy, consumer-protection, tax, security, and accessibility review for each market it serves.
